column2: The robot's brain
The brain holds the touchscreen, the sound and the internet connection. Each module is tested on its own first, then the brain is connected to the body.
Brain pins (ESP32-S3)

1 5V block (red) and GND (black). In run mode, 5 V from LM2596 #1 goes in here. While USB is plugged in, your board's 5V pin reads only about 1.5-2.9 V (you measured it), so do not use it as a 5 V source on the table.
2 3V3 block and GND: the 3.3 V source for the display, microphone and speaker while on the table.
3 and 4: three columns for each GPIO. Yellow = S (signal), red = 3.3 V, black = GND. The GPIO name is printed on the edge: IO4, IO5, ... IO21.
5 Straight yellow header near the socket: a direct connection to the S3 pins as they are.
6 DC jack 6.5-9 V: not used. 7 USB symbol: the S3's USB-C port faces this way when installed.

Build the brain
Every stage in this part uses table mode: the S3 gets power from USB, and the modules from the 3V3 block.
Set up the S3 and check PSRAM
Your ESP32-S3 N16R8. Two USB-C ports: one goes through a USB-serial chip (COM), the other is the chip's built-in USB.

Enabled if the cable is in the chip's built-in USB port (the upload log says USB mode: USB-Serial/JTAG); Disabled if it is in the UART/COM port (the log says USB mode: UART)
Choosing the wrong PSRAM is the most common reason the brain code fails later.
You see Flash: 16 MB and PSRAM: 8388608 byte (about 8 million).
OK to lock in The Arduino Tools settings (OPI PSRAM, Huge APP) and the S3 staying plugged into its expansion board: the two go up to level 3 as one unit.
Not yet The S3 board is not bolted down yet. On the robot it uses 10 mm nylon standoffs, with the USB-C port facing sideways (Part 6 Stage 4).
PSRAM 0: the PSRAM menu is not set to OPI PSRAM.
Upload fails with "Connecting...": hold the BOOT button on the S3, press RST once, release BOOT, then upload again.

Upload succeeds but the Serial Monitor is empty: look at the upload log in the Output tab. If it says USB mode: USB-Serial/JTAG, you are using the chip's built-in USB port: set USB CDC On Boot to Enabled, upload again, and reopen the Serial Monitor. If it says USB mode: UART, leave it Disabled. The other port does not show up on the computer: try another data cable, or install the UART chip's driver.
TFT display and touch
The front of your display: 14 pins on the left, 4 SD holes on the right.
The back: pin names from T_IRQ (top) to VCC (bottom), full-size SD slot.

Why this way? The display, touch and SD share the same three wires (SCK, MOSI, MISO). The ESP32 chooses which one to talk to by pulling that device's CS pin low. That is why every device has its own CS wire.
OK to lock in The wiring layout on breadboard 2 (SPI bus in columns 2, 5, 8 and the display pins). This breadboard goes up to level 3 together with its wires.

Not yet The display is not bolted down yet. On the robot it lies facing up on 20 mm standoffs, and the wires going to its pins are under the display, so they must already be plugged in before the display is bolted down.
Display is only white: RESET, DC or CS is not connected, or SCK/MOSI are swapped.
Inverted colors (black becomes white): in the code, change c.invert = false to true. Red and blue swapped: type w in step 2.
Picture shifted or streaked: the SPI wires are too long. Use 10-20 cm wires, or lower freq_write to 20000000.
The SD card on the back of the display
The Serial Monitor prints the SD size and the file list, and the display shows the file names.
OK to lock in The four soldered SD header pins, the FAT32 format and the songs on the card.
Not yet Nothing is mounted to the plate at this stage.
SD GAGAL: format as FAT32 (not exFAT), check SD_CS to IO21, try another card. Cards above 32 GB are usually exFAT.
The display works but the SD fails only when the display is on: the display's SDO(MISO) may be connected. Unplug it.
Your boxed speaker. The round 8 Ω 3 W speaker is the spare.
Your MAX98357A: 4-8 Ω, 3 W, Vin 2.5-5.5 V.

Why this way? The MAX98357A receives digital sound (I2S) and amplifies it straight to the speaker. GAIN pin left open = 9 dB gain, SD pin left open = on. On the finished robot, Vin is moved to 5 V to make it louder.
You hear do-re-mi-fa-sol and then a one-second pause, repeating.
OK to lock in The speaker wires clamped in the ⊕ and ⊖ terminals.
Not yet The MAX98357A Vin is still on the 3.3 V rail. On the robot it is moved to the S3 board's 5V pin (Part 6 Stage 6). The speaker is not strapped to the plate yet (Part 6 Stage 4).
Silent: check that BCLK/LRC/DIN are not swapped and the speaker wires are clamped firmly in the terminal (not the insulation).
Crackling: the GND wire is not firm enough, or the data wires are too long.

Why this way? L/R to GND makes the microphone send sound on the left channel. The code reads only the left channel. The microphone and speaker use two separate I2S channels, so each can be set on its own.
The line in the Serial Plotter is low when quiet (tens to hundreds) and jumps to the thousands when you clap or speak.
OK to lock in The soldered INMP441 header pins, with the sound hole left uncovered.
Not yet VDD stays on 3.3 V. Do not move it to 5 V in run mode like the speaker's Vin: the INMP441 must not get 5 V.
Large numbers even when quiet: the GND wire came loose.
Connect the brain to the body (UART)
One board's TX always goes to the other board's RX (crossed).
You see badan: PONG and data lines badan: D .... The M command moves the wheels.
OK to lock in The UART pairs: IO17 to D16, IO18 to D17, G to G. On the robot it is exactly the same, only with longer wires.
Not yet The 20 cm jumper wires on the table are not final: on the robot the UART wires are longer and joined with F-F and M-F (Part 6 Stage 4).
No reply: TX-RX are not crossed, GND is not connected, or the body does not yet have robot_badan.ino.
Strange characters: both boards must be at 115200 (already in the code).

Pins marked ✕ (SDO(MISO) and T_IRQ) are left without wires. The red and blue lines of breadboard 2 are themselves powered by the 3V3 and G pins of the S3 expansion board (step 2).
The Serial Monitor prints LULUS: kalibrasi tepat. (calibration passed) and TERSIMPAN (saved). The yellow stroke appears right under the stylus, and tapped dots land inside all five circles.
Text looks mirrored: in step 2 try another number from 0 to 7. Only part of the screen is drawn (a full color only covers about ¾ of the screen, text is cut off): wrong panel type, type g in step 2.
Strokes appear somewhere else or slanted: type k and Enter to recalibrate, and press the exact center point of the + mark, not the end of its lines.
Touch does not respond: test step 3 shows which wire to check. Usually T_CS to IO14 or T_DO to column 8.
